titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Moses' Rod and the Cross: Amalek and the Bitter Water (ch. 98, part 2 of 2)
part: ch. 98, part 2 of 2 — Moses' Rod and the Cross: Amalek and the Bitter Water
about: The chronicler continues reading Moses' rod as the cross: the water turned to blood, the darkness, the rod that changes between dry and living, and the stretched hand. He then reads the battle with Amalek (Exodus 17) as the war of believers against demons, with Aaron and Hur as the two thieves, the bitter water of Marah as sweetened by the sign of the cross, and ends with David's prophecies of the nailing and the vinegar.

sentences.t: ወበትረ ፡ ሙሴኒ ፡ እንተ ፡ ባቲ ፡ በዘገብረ ፡ ተኣምረ ፡ ትተረጐም ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፡ በዘአድኀኖ ፡ ለአዳም ፡ ወለደቂቁ ፡ እምሥቃየ ፡ አጋንንት ፤
sentences.l: And-rod-of Moses-also, which in-her by-what-he-did wonders, is-interpreted wood-of cross, by-what-he-saved-him Adam and-sons-his from-torment-of demons;
sentences.i: And the rod of Moses too, through which he worked wonders, is interpreted as the wood of the cross, by which Adam and his children were saved from the torment of the demons;
sentences.n: Read this as the start of the typological argument: each act of Moses' rod is matched by an act of Christ's cross. ወበትረ is ወ- 'and' + በትር 'rod' in the construct state (before ሙሴ); -ኒ on ሙሴኒ is the emphatic 'also'. እንተ ባቲ is the feminine relative 'which' (agreeing with በትር, a feminine noun) + በ- with -ቲ 'her', 'in which, through which'; በዘገብረ is በ- + ዘ- 'what' + ገብረ 'he did'. ትተረጐም 'she/it is interpreted' (3fs imperfect, passive, agreeing with the rod); the ዕፀ መስቀል 'wood of the cross' is what it is read as. በዘአድኀኖ 'by that by which he saved him' is a loose relative: the subject, Christ, is only understood. ወለደቂቁ is ወ- + ለ- (marking the object) + 'his sons'; እምሥቃየ 'from the torment of' (እም- + construct). This part begins mid-paragraph of the chapter (continuing ch. 98 part 1), so unit 0 has no paragraph mark.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ዘበጠ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ማየ ፡ ተከዜ ፡ ወረሰያ ፡ ደመ ፡ ወቀተለ ፡ ዓሣቲሆሙ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ክርስቶስኒ ፡ በመስቀሉ ፡ ቀተሎ ፡ ለሞት ፡ ወአውፅኦሙ ፡ እምውስተ ፡ ሲኦል ፤
sentences.l: And-as Moses struck with-her the-water-of Tekezé and-made-it blood and-killed fish-their, likewise Christ-also by-his-cross killed death and-brought-them-out from-within Sheol;
sentences.i: And as Moses struck the water of the Tekezé with it and made it blood and killed their fish, so Christ also by his cross killed death and brought them out of Sheol;
sentences.n: ወበከመ 'and as' (ወ- + በ- + ከመ) opens the 'as ... so' comparison that runs through the part; ከማሁ 'likewise' answers it, and -ኒ again means 'also'. ዘበጠ 'he struck'. ተከዜ is the Tekezé, the great Ethiopian river; the chronicler sets the Nile plague (Exodus 7:20-21) on his own country's river. ወረሰያ 'and he made it' (ረሰየ, 3ms perfect + -ኣ 'it', the rod's water taken as feminine or collective). ዓሣቲሆሙ 'their fish' (plural ዓሣት + -ሆሙ). ቀተሎ ለሞት 'killed death' (ቀተለ 'killed' + -ኦ, doubled by ለ- marking the object), and ሲኦል is Sheol, the underworld the dead were held in.

sentences.t: ወበከ ፡ መ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ዘበጠ ፡ በበትሩ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ነፋሳት ፡ ወጸልመ ፡ ኵላ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ እስከ ፡ ፫ ፡ ዕለት ፡ ወ፫ ፡ ሌሊት ፡ ጽልመት ፡ ዘያርመሰምስ ፡ እስከ ፡ ኢይትነሥኡ ፡ እምስካቢሆሙ ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ ክርስቶስኒ ፡ ተሰቂሎ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ዕፅ ፡ አብርህ ፡ ጽልመተ ፡ አልባበ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወተንሥአ ፡ እምዉታን ፡ በሣልስት ፡ ዕለት ፡ ወሣልስት ፡ ሌሊት ፤
sentences.l: And-as(?) Moses struck with-his-rod into winds and-was-dark all land-of Egypt until 3 day and-3 night, darkness which-gropes (?) until not-they-rose from-beds-their, and-likewise Christ-also, hanged upon wood, lit darkness-of hearts-of man, and-rose from-the-dead on-third day and-third night;
sentences.i: And as Moses struck with his rod into the winds, and all the land of Egypt grew dark for three days and three nights, a darkness that could be felt (?), so that they did not rise from their beds, so Christ also, hanged upon the wood, lit the darkness of human hearts, and rose from the dead on the third day and the third night;
sentences.n: Source slip kept as printed: ወበከ ፡ መ ፡ ሙሴ, where the printer split ወበከመ 'and as' into three words; read it as ወበከመ. Plague of darkness, Exodus 10:21-23. ዘበጠ በበትሩ 'who struck with his rod' (the second በ- is 'with, by means of'); ውስተ ነፋሳት 'into the winds', ነፋሳት plural of ነፋስ. ወጸልመ 'and it grew dark' (ጸልመ, 3ms perfect); ኵላ ምድረ ግብጽ 'all the land of Egypt' (ኵላ accusative, ምድረ construct). The numerals: ፫ ፡ ዕለት 'three days', ወ፫ ፡ ሌሊት 'and three nights', the noun singular after a number. ዘያርመሰምስ is a relative + a four-letter verb, 3ms imperfect, said of the darkness; the sense 'be groped in, be felt' (Exodus 10:21) is my reading (?). እስከ ኢይትነሥኡ 'until they did not rise', here 'so that'. ተሰቂሎ 'having been hanged' (ተሰቅለ, converb), አብርህ 'he lit' (3ms perfect, causative of በርሀ); ጽልመተ አልባበ ሰብእ is a construct chain. በሣልስት ዕለት 'on the third day' (ordinal ሣልስ + fem. -ት).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ በትረ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ሚጦተ ፡ ወወልጦተ ፡ በቃለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብስት ፡ ኮነት ፡ ዘነፍስ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ነፍስ ፡ ኮነት ፡ ይብስተ ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ ክርስቶስኒ ፡ በዕፀ ፡ መስቀሉ ፡ ረሰየ ፡ ሕይወተ ፡ ለሕዝበ ፡ ክርስቲያን ፡ ለእለ ፡ አምኑ ፡ ቦቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-as rod-of Moses became turning and-changing by-word-of God, while dry it-became that-of soul(living), and-again while soul(living) it-became dryness; and-likewise Christ-also, by-wood-of his-cross made life for-people-of Christian, for-those-who believed in-him;
sentences.i: And as the rod of Moses underwent a turning and a changing at the word of God, so that dry wood became living, and again, being living, became dry; so Christ also, by the wood of his cross, made life for the Christian people, for those who have believed in him;
sentences.n: The rod that became a serpent and then a rod again (Exodus 4:3-4; 7:10-12). በትረ ሙሴ 'rod of Moses' (construct); ኮነ ሚጦተ ወወልጦተ 'became a turning and a changing' (two verbal nouns in the accusative, ሚጦት and ወልጦት; ኮነ is 3ms though the rod is fem., then ኮነት 3fs). በቃለ 'at the word of' (በ- + construct). The pair ይብስት / ዘነፍስ is my reading: ይብስት 'dryness, dry' (ይብስ 'dry') against ዘነፍስ 'that of soul', i.e. living, ነፍስ 'soul, life'; I take እንዘ ይብስት ... ዘነፍስ as 'while dry ... living' (?). በዕፀ መስቀሉ 'by the wood of his cross'; ለሕዝበ ክርስቲያን 'for the Christian people' (ለ- + construct); ለእለ አምኑ ቦቱ 'for those who believed in him' (እለ 'those who', አምኑ 3mp perfect, ቦቱ = በ + 'him').

sentences.t: ረሰየ ፡ በትእምርተ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሰደዲ ፡ መንፈሰ ፡ አጋንንት ፡ እስመ ፡ ተውላጠ ፡ ኮኑ ፡ አጋንንት ፡ ወክርስቲያን ፤
sentences.l: He-made by-sign-of cross that he-might-drive-out spirit-of demons, for exchanged they-became demons and-Christian;
sentences.i: He did this by the sign of the cross, so that he might drive out the spirit of the demons, for the demons and the Christians had changed places;
sentences.n: ረሰየ 'he made (it so)', the object left to be understood; በትእምርተ 'by the sign of' (በ- + construct). ከመ ይሰደዲ 'that he might drive out': a purpose clause with a jussive, spelled ይሰደዲ as printed (the regular jussive would be ይሰድድ, so the form may be corrupt or a variant (?)). መንፈሰ አጋንንት 'spirit of demons' (construct). እስመ 'for, because'. ተውላጠ ኮኑ 'they became exchanged' (ተውላጠ a participle or noun 'changed, exchanged' + ኮኑ 3mp perfect of ኮነ); the exchange is explained in the next unit: the demons, once spirits, fell; Christians, who were not, become spiritual.

sentences.t: እሙንቱ ፡ እንዘ ፡ መንፈሳዊያን ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ኅሱራነ ፡ በተዐድዎ ፡ ትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚኦሙ ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ስዲዳነ ፡ በኀይለ ፡ መስቀሉ ፡ ወንሕነኒ ፡ ኮነ ፡ መንፈሳዊያነ ፡ በነሢአ ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ ወደሙ ፡ ህየንቴሆሙ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ተሰዲ ፡ መንፈሳዊያን ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ንሕነ ፡ ሰባሕያነ ፡ እለ ፡ አመነ ፡ በመስቀሉ ፡ ወበትንሣኤሁ ፡ ቅድስት ፤
sentences.l: They, while spiritual ones, became lacking by-their-transgressing command-of their-Lord, became driven-out by-power-of his-cross; and-we-also became spiritual-ones by-taking body-his and-blood-his in-place-of-them, of-those-who they-were-driven-out spiritual-ones, and-became we praisers who believed in-his-cross and-in-resurrection-his holy;
sentences.i: They, although they were spiritual beings, became deficient by transgressing the command of their Lord, and became exiles through the power of his cross; and we also have become spiritual, by receiving his body and blood in place of those spiritual beings who were driven out, and we have become praisers, we who believe in his cross and in his holy resurrection;
sentences.n: This explains the exchange of the previous unit: the fallen spirits (demons) lost their place; believers take it. እሙንቱ 'they' (3mp pronoun); እንዘ መንፈሳዊያን 'while spiritual ones'; ኮኑ ኅሱራነ 'they became deficient' (accusative plural of ኅሱር, predicate); በተዐድዎ ትእዛዘ 'by transgressing the commandment of' (በ- + verbal noun + construct); እግዚኦሙ 'their Lord' (እግዚእ + -ሙ). ስዲዳነ 'driven out, exiled' (accusative plural of a passive participle, a reading from the context (?)). The verb ኮነ is printed in the 3ms form with plural subjects in ወንሕነኒ ኮነ መንፈሳዊያነ 'and we also became spiritual ones' and ወኮነ ንሕነ ሰባሕያነ 'and we became praisers' (the regular 1cp would be ኮንነ); kept as printed. ሰባሕያነ 'praisers' (?) from a root of praise; I read ሰባሕያን as 'those who give praise, glorifiers'. በነሢአ 'by taking' (infinitive); ህየንቴሆሙ 'in their place'; ለእለ ተሰዲ is printed as is: 'of those who were driven out' (ተሰዲ read as a passive of ሰደደ, 3mp perfect, a short spelling (?)); እለ አመነ 'who believed', singular verb after plural relative, as in earlier parts. ቅድስት 'holy', feminine, agreeing with ትንሣኤ 'resurrection'.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ዘበጠ ፡ አድባረ ፡ ወአምጽአ ፡ መቅሠፍተ ፡ በትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ሰፊሖ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ምስለ ፡ በትሩ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ክርስቶስኒ ፡ አውፅኦሙ ፡ ለአጋንንት ፡ እምላዕለ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ በኀይለ ፡ መስቀሉ ፡ ሰፊሖ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፤
sentences.l: And-as Moses struck mountains and-brought scourge by-command-of God, stretching hand-his with rod-his, likewise Christ-also brought-them-out demons from-upon man by-power-of his-cross, stretching hand-his upon wood-of cross;
sentences.i: And as Moses struck the mountains and brought a scourge at the command of God, stretching out his hand with his rod, so Christ also brought the demons out from men by the power of his cross, stretching out his hand upon the wood of the cross;
sentences.n: ዘበጠ አድባረ 'who struck mountains' (አድባረ accusative plural of ደብር; the allusion is unclear, perhaps the plagues generally or the rock, so the reading of 'mountains' is as printed (?)); ወአምጽአ መቅሠፍተ 'and he brought a scourge' (ወ- + causative perfect + accusative); በትእዛዘ 'at the command of'. ሰፊሖ is a converb, 'having stretched / stretching' (ሰፍሐ), twice: first of Moses, then of Christ, the stretched hand being the link between the two. ለአጋንንት is ለ- marking the object; እምላዕለ 'from upon' (እም- + ላዕለ).

sentences.t: ሶበ ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ዝብጥ ፡ በበትርከ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ዕትብ ፡ በማዕተበ ፡ መስቀሉ ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: When said-to-him God to-Moses 'Strike with-your-rod', this saying: 'Seal with-seal-of cross-his, of-Christ', saying;
sentences.i: When God said to Moses, 'Strike with your rod,' this means: 'Mark with the seal of Christ's cross,' that is to say;
sentences.n: ብሂል 'saying, that is' is the interpreter's formula that closes each reading; here it brackets the interpretation. The sentence has no main verb (the ሶበ 'when' clause is resumed in the next unit). ዝብጥ 'strike!' (imperative, 2ms, of ዘበጠ; spelled with ብ as printed); ዕትብ 'seal! mark!' (imperative of ዐተበ); ማዕተበ 'seal of' (construct); ለክርስቶስ 'of Christ' (ለ- marking the possessor after the anticipatory suffix on መስቀሉ 'his cross'). So striking is read as signing with the cross.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ስፋሕ ፡ እዴከ ፡ ዝኒ ፡ ብሂል ፡ ከመ ፡ በስፍሐተ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ አድኀነነ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ እምተቀንዮ ፡ ለጸላኢ ፡ ወወሀበነ ፡ ሕይወተ ፡ እንቲአሁ ፡ በስፍሐተ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ብሂል ።
sentences.l: And-when said-to-him God to-Moses 'Stretch hand-your', this-also saying, that by-stretching-of hand-his saved-us Christ from-service(?) for-the-enemy, and-gave-us life his-own by-stretching-of hand-his upon wood-of cross, saying.
sentences.i: And when God said to Moses, 'Stretch out your hand,' this too means that by the stretching out of his hands Christ saved us from servitude to the enemy (?) and gave us his own life, by the stretching out of his hands upon the wood of the cross.
sentences.n: ስፋሕ 'stretch!' (imperative, 2ms of ሰፍሐ); ዝኒ 'this too' (ዝ + -ኒ). The ከመ 'that' clause gives the meaning: በስፍሐተ 'by the stretching of' (በ- + construct); አድኀነነ 'he saved us' (3ms perfect + -ነ); እምተቀንዮ 'from servitude' (?): ተቀንዮ is a noun of the root ቀነየ 'serve, be subject', my reading from the root, with ለጸላኢ 'to the enemy' (ለ- 'to', ጸላኢ 'enemy') (?). ወወሀበነ 'and he gave us'; እንቲአሁ 'his own' (fem. relative-possessive agreeing with ሕይወት 'life'). The unit ends with ። and closes the paragraph.

sentences.t: ወአመኒ ፡ ይጸብኡ ፡ ዐማልቅ ፡ ምስለ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ዐርገ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ደብር ፡ ወአሮን ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ዐርጉ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይጸልዩ ፡ እስመ ፡ ተኀየሉ ፡ ዐማሌቅ ፡ ወአዘዞ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ስፋሕ ፡ እዴከ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይረክቡ ፡ ኀይለ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-at-the-time-when they-fought Amalek with Israel, went-up Moses into mountain and-Aaron with-him they-went-up that they-might-pray, for were-strong Amalek; and-commanded-him God Moses and-said-to-him 'Stretch hand-your until they-find strength-of Israel(?)';
sentences.i: And when Amalek fought against Israel, Moses went up onto the mountain, and Aaron with him, so that they might pray, for Amalek had grown strong; and God commanded Moses and said to him, 'Stretch out your hand until they gain the strength of Israel (?)';
sentences.n: Exodus 17:8-13. ወአመኒ ይጸብኡ: ወ- 'and' + አመ 'at the time of' + -ኒ, with the plural verb ይጸብኡ 'they fight' (3mp imperfect) although ዐማልቅ is singular in form, a collective. Source slip kept as printed: ዐማልቅ for ዐማሌቅ 'Amalek' (the ሌ is dropped; the same name is spelled ዐማሌቅ later in the unit). ዐርገ ሙሴ 'Moses went up'; ዐርጉ 'they went up' (3mp perfect); ከመ ይጸልዩ 'that they might pray' (jussive 3mp); እስመ ተኀየሉ 'for they had grown strong' (ተኀየለ, 3mp, collective). ወአዘዞ ... ወይቤሎ 'and he commanded him ... and said to him'. The last clause is uncertain (?): እስከ ይረክቡ ኀይለ እስራኤል 'until they find the strength of Israel' has a plural verb but no clear subject; it may mean 'until Israel's forces prevail'.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ኦሪት ፡ ኮና ፡ ርቡባተ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ እስከ ፡ ዕርበተ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ አላ ፡ ባሕቱ ፡ ክቡዳት ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ የዐፅቦ ፡ አውረደ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ እምዘ ፡ ሰፍሐ ፡ ይትዌጽዑ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወይመውእዎሙ ፡ ፀሮሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-says in-Torah: were light(?) hands-his of-Moses until setting-of sun, but however heavy hands-his of-Moses; and-when it-wearies-him he-lowered hand-his from-what he-stretched, are-routed(?) Israel and-conquer-them their-enemies;
sentences.i: And he says in the Torah that the hands of Moses were steady (?) until the setting of the sun, but nevertheless the hands of Moses were heavy; and whenever he grew weary and let his hand down from where he had stretched it, Israel were routed (?) and their enemies conquered them;
sentences.n: The chronicler summarises Exodus 17:11-12 loosely ('in the Torah'). ወይቤ 'and he said / says' (3ms perfect ይቤ; the subject is the Scripture's author); ኮና 'they two were' (3fd perfect, agreeing with the 'two hands', fem. dual in sense) with ርቡባተ 'steady, light, soft (?)' (adjective, plural fem.), meaning uncertain (?). ዕርበተ ፀሐይ 'the setting of the sun'; አላ ባሕቱ 'but nevertheless'; ክቡዳት 'heavy' (plural fem.). ሶበ የዐፅቦ 'when it wearies him' (የዐፅቦ 3ms imperfect + -ኦ); ይትዌጽዑ 'are routed, overcome' (?) a reading from the passive stem ተ-; ይመውእዎሙ 'they conquer them' (ሞአ 'conquer'), ፀሮሙ 'their enemies' (ፀር + -ሙ, subject).

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ያሌዕል ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ወይሰፍሕ ፡ በርቱዕ ፡ ይትመውኡ ፡ ዐማሌቅ ፡ ወይሰድድዎሙ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወይመው ፡ እዎሙ ፡ ለፀሮሙ ፡ ዓማሌቅ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-raises hand-his and-stretches in-uprightness, are-conquered Amalek and-pursue-them Israel and-conquer them their-enemy Amalek;
sentences.i: And when he lifted his hand and stretched it out straight, Amalek were conquered and Israel pursued them and overcame their enemy Amalek;
sentences.n: Source slip kept as printed: ይመው ፡ እዎሙ, where the printer split ይመውእዎሙ 'they conquer them' into two words; read as one. ያሌዕል 'he raises' and ይሰፍሕ 'he stretches' (3ms imperfect, repeated action; I turn them into 'when he lifted', a habitual past). በርቱዕ 'in uprightness, straight' (በ- + adjective). ይትመውኡ 'they are conquered' (passive, ተ-stem of ሞአ); ይሰድድዎሙ 'they pursue them, drive them off' (ሰደደ + -ዎሙ). ዓማሌቅ is written with ዓ here, a variant of ዐማሌቅ.

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ርእዩ ፡ አሮን ፡ ወሆር ፡ ነደቁ ፡ እብነ ፡ በየማኑ ፡ ወበፀጋሙ ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ወአፅግዑ ፡ እደወ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ አእባን ፡ ዘነደቁ ፡ አሮን ፡ እንተ ፡ የማኑ ፡ ወሆር ፡ እንተ ፡ ፀጋሙ ፡ ወአኀዝዎ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መታክፍቲሆሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያግብእ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ እምዘሰፍሖ ።
sentences.l: And-this when they-saw Aaron and-Hur set-up stone at-his-right and-at-his-left, of-Moses, and-they-set-down(?) hands-of Moses upon stones which set-up Aaron, that of his-right, and-Hur, that of his-left, and-held-him upon their-shoulders that not-he-should-bring-back hand-his from-what-he-stretched-it.
sentences.i: And when Aaron and Hur saw this, they set up a stone on Moses' right and on his left, and they laid the hands of Moses upon the stones that Aaron and Hur had set up, Aaron's on the right and Hur's on the left, and they held him on their shoulders, so that he would not bring his hand back from what he had stretched out.
sentences.n: Exodus 17:12: in the Bible Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands and a stone is put under him to sit on; here the stones carry the hands. ሶበ ርእዩ 'when they saw' (3mp perfect); ነደቁ 'they set up' (3mp perfect, ነደቀ 'set up, plant'); እብነ 'a stone' (accusative); በየማኑ ወበፀጋሙ 'at his right and at his left' (the suffix -ኑ, -ሙ stand for -ሁ 'his' after the vowel). ወአፅግዑ 'and they set down, rested (?)' (causative stem; the exact verb is uncertain (?)); እደወ 'hands of' (a construct plural, as printed). እንተ የማኑ 'that of his right' is the fem. relative standing for 'the one on his right'. ወአኀዝዎ 'and they held him / it' (አኀዘ 'hold', + -ዎ); መታክፍቲሆሙ 'their shoulders'. ከመ ኢያግብእ 'that he not bring back' (jussive negative). እምዘሰፍሖ 'from what he had stretched' (እም- + ዘ- + ሰፍሐ + -ኦ). The unit ends at ።, the end of the paragraph.

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ እፌክር ፡ ለክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-this I-interpret to-you;
sentences.i: And this I explain to you;
sentences.n: A new paragraph begins; the chronicler turns from narrative to his own interpretation. እፌክር is 1cs imperfect of ፈከረ 'interpret, explain'; the narrator uses the same root as ፍካሬ 'interpretation' elsewhere; ለክሙ 'to you' (ለ- + -ክሙ 2mp).

sentences.t: ፀብአ ፡ ዐማሌቅሰ ፡ ምስለ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ፀብአ ፡ መሀይምናን ፡ ምስለ ፡ አጋንንት ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወዘእንበለ ፡ ይሰቀል ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ሞእዎሙ ፡ ለቀደምት ፤
sentences.l: War-of Amalek-as-for with Israel war-of believers with demons it-was, and-before was-crucified Christ they-conquered-them the-ancients;
sentences.i: As for the war of Amalek against Israel, it was the war of believers against demons, and before Christ was crucified they conquered the ancients;
sentences.n: The allegory is stated plainly: Amalek is the demons, Israel the believers. ፀብአ 'war of' (construct); -ሰ on ዐማሌቅሰ is 'as for, but'; ውእቱ 'it was' (copula). ወዘእንበለ ይሰቀል 'and before he was crucified' (ዘእንበለ + 3ms imperfect passive subjunctive). ሞእዎሙ is kept as printed (3mp perfect of ሞአ 'conquer' + -ሙ 'them', with the ሞእ- spelling of the stem); the subject is the demons and the object is ለቀደምት 'the ancients, those of old' (ለ- marking the object), so the sense is that the demons held the old order before the cross.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ሰፍሐ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፡ በእንተ ፡ ኀጢአተ ፡ አዳም ፡ ወደቂቁ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ሰፍሐ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ወተቀነወ ፡ እራኁ ፡ ሞእዎሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ይትዐተቡ ፡ በመስቀሉ ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-stretched hand-his upon wood-of cross for sin-of Adam and-his-sons, and-when he-stretched hand-his and-was-nailed his-body(?), conquered-them those-who are-sealed by-his-cross, of-Christ;
sentences.i: And when he stretched out his hand on the wood of the cross for the sin of Adam and his children, and when he stretched out his hand and was nailed (?), those who are sealed by the cross of Christ conquered them;
sentences.n: Here the picture reverses: after the cross, it is the believers who conquer the demons. ሞእዎሙ is 'they conquered them' with subject እለ ይትዐተቡ 'those who are sealed' (ይትዐተቡ 3mp imperfect, passive/reflexive of ዐተበ 'mark, seal', the sign of the cross); the same ሞእዎሙ is used in the previous unit with the demons as subject. ኀጢአተ አዳም is a construct chain. ተቀነወ 'was nailed, pierced' (ተቀነወ 3ms perfect, passive of ቀነወ 'nail'; the nouns are ቅንዋት 'nails'). እራኁ is unresolved (?): I do not know the word; it follows the verb as if it were an accusative of the part nailed (his … 'hand, side, feet'), but the form is not known to me. It is left unglossed in the English.

sentences.t: ስፍሐ ፡ እዴሁ ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ ስቅለቱ ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ወዘነደቁ ፡ አእባን ፡ አሮን ፡ ወሆር ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ወቅንዋት ፤
sentences.l: Stretching-of hand-his of-Moses is-interpreted crucifixion-his of-Christ, and-what they-set-up stones Aaron and-Hur is-interpreted wood-of cross and-nails;
sentences.i: The stretching out of the hands of Moses is interpreted as the crucifixion of Christ, and what Aaron and Hur set up, the stones, is interpreted as the wood of the cross and the nails;
sentences.n: The interpretation proper. ስፍሐ 'stretching of' (construct of ስፍሐት); ለሙሴ and ለክርስቶስ are ለ- marking the possessor after the anticipatory suffix (እዴሁ ለሙሴ 'Moses' hand'; ስቅለቱ ለክርስቶስ 'Christ's crucifixion'). ይተረጐም 'is interpreted', as in the first unit. ዘነደቁ አእባን 'what they set up, the stones'; ዕፀ መስቀል ወቅንዋት 'wood of the cross and the nails' (ቅንዋት plural of ቅንዋት, nails).

sentences.t: ወአሮን ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ በፈያታዊ ፡ ዘየማን ፡ ወሆር ፡ በፈያታዊ ፡ ዘፀጋም ፡ ወዐማሌቅ ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ በአጋንንት ፡ ወንጉሦሙ ፡ ለዐማሌቅ ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ በሰይጣን ፤
sentences.l: And-Aaron is-interpreted as-thief at-the-right and-Hur as-thief at-the-left, and-Amalek is-interpreted as-demons and-king-their of-Amalek is-interpreted as-Satan;
sentences.i: And Aaron is interpreted as the thief on the right, and Hur as the thief on the left, and Amalek is interpreted as the demons, and the king of Amalek as Satan;
sentences.n: The two thieves crucified with Christ (Luke 23:32-43); here the two sides are matched to Aaron and Hur. ፈያታዊ ዘየማን 'the robber of the right' (ዘ- relative + noun); በ- is 'as, by means of' in ይተረጐም በ- 'is interpreted as'. ወንጉሦሙ ለዐማሌቅ 'and their king, of Amalek' (ንጉሥ + -ሙ, anticipating ለ-).

sentences.t: ወአሜሃ ፡ ዘተመውኡ ፡ ውእቶሙ ፡ በትንሣኤሁ ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ወበመስቀሉ ፡ ሞእናሆሙ ፡ ለአጋንንት ፡ ወለሰይጣን ፡ ወካ ፡ ዕበ ፡ አመ ፡ ይወፅኡ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እምግብጽ ፡ ወፅኡ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ማይ ፡ መሪር ፡ ወኀጥኡ ፡ ዘይሰትዩ ፡ እምረተ ፡ ማዩ ፡ ወቀዳሚ ፡ ነጐርጓር ፡ አንጐርጐሩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ምረተ ፡ ማይ ፤
sentences.l: And-then they-who were-conquered they, by-resurrection-his of-Christ and-by-his-cross we-conquered-them demons and-Satan; and-again(slip) when they-come-out Israel from-Egypt they-went-out into water bitter and-lacked(?) what-they-might-drink from-bitterness-of its-water, and-first murmuring they-murmured because-of bitterness-of water;
sentences.i: And then, those who were conquered were they: by the resurrection of Christ and by his cross we conquered the demons and Satan. And again, when Israel came out of Egypt, they went out to bitter water and lacked (?) anything to drink because of the bitterness of its water, and at first they murmured on account of the bitterness of the water;
sentences.n: Source slip kept as printed: ወካ ፡ ዕበ for ወካዕበ 'and again', split into two words. ወአሜሃ 'and then'; ዘተመውኡ ውእቶሙ 'those who were conquered, they' (ዘ- relative + 3mp passive perfect + 3mp pronoun), the demons. ሞእናሆሙ 'we conquered them' (ሞአ 1cp perfect + -ሆሙ); ለአጋንንት ወለሰይጣን with object ለ-. Then Exodus 15:22-24, Marah. አመ ይወፅኡ 'when they come out' (3mp imperfect, narrative present). ወኀጥኡ ዘይሰትዩ: ኀጥኡ is taken as 3mp perfect of 'lack, be without' with ዘይሰትዩ 'what they might drink' (?), uncertain. ማዩ 'its water' (ማይ + -ሁ); ምረተ 'bitterness of'. ነጐርጓር 'a murmur, grumbling' (noun) with አንጐርጐሩ 'they murmured', a cognate-accusative figure; ቀዳሚ 'first, at first'.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ ንሣእ ፡ በትረከ ፡ ወደይ ፡ ውስቴቱ ፡ ወዕተቦ ፡ ይምነ ፡ ወፅግመ ፤
sentences.l: And-said-to-him God to-Moses 'Take your-rod and-put (it) in-it, and-seal-it to-the-right and-to-the-left;
sentences.i: And God said to Moses, 'Take your rod and put it into it, and mark it to the right and to the left;
sentences.n: Marah, Exodus 15:23-25 (where God shows Moses a piece of wood); here the rod is put into the water and the water is marked, the cross-sign to right and left. ንሣእ 'take!' (imperative, 2ms); ወደይ 'put!' (imperative of ወደየ); ውስቴቱ 'in it' (ውስተ + -ቱ); ዕተቦ 'seal it, mark it' (imperative of ዐተበ, as in the earlier ዕትብ + -ኦ); ይምነ and ፅግመ are the right and left taken adverbially. The quotation is not closed in the text, being continued in the interpreter's comment that follows.

sentences.t: ወርኢ ፡ በዝንቱ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይኩን ፡ ጥዑመ ፡ እመ ፡ ኢኮነኑ ፡ ጥዑመ ፤
sentences.l: And-see by-this: when said-to-him God 'Let-it-be sweet', whether not-was-it sweet?
sentences.i: And see by this: when God said to him, 'Let it be sweet,' was it not sweet already? (?)
sentences.n: The line is difficult. ወርኢ 'and see!' (imperative, 2ms of ርእየ); በዝንቱ 'by this'; ይኩን 'let it be' (jussive, 3ms of ኮነ); እመ ኢኮነኑ ጥዑመ is 'whether it was not sweet?' (እመ 'if, whether' + ኢኮነ 'was not' + the question particle -ኑ): the speaker means that God's word alone would have sweetened the water (?), so the rod and the sign are there for a meaning beyond that, as the next unit says.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ያርኢ ፡ ከመ ፡ በትእምርተ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ይሤኒ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ወማይ ፡ መሪር ፡ ይከውን ፡ ጥዑመ ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ዘማሰነ ፡ በኀይለ ፡ መስቀሉ ፡ ለኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ይከውን ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ወአዳመ ።
sentences.l: But he-shows that by-sign-of cross is-made-beautiful all, and-water bitter becomes sweet, and-everything which-was-spoiled by-power-of cross-his of-Jesus Christ will-be good and-pleasing.
sentences.i: But he shows that everything is made beautiful by the sign of the cross, and bitter water becomes sweet, and everything that was spoiled will become good and pleasing by the power of the cross of Jesus Christ.
sentences.n: ወባሕቱ 'but' (ወ- + ባሕቱ); ያርኢ 'he shows' (3ms imperfect, causative of ርእየ); ከመ 'that'. ይሤኒ 'it is made beautiful' (3ms imperfect of ሠነየ, read as passive 'becomes beautiful'); ይከውን 'becomes' (3ms imperfect of ኮነ). ዘማሰነ 'what was spoiled' (ዘ- + ማሰነ 'perished, decayed'), the sense taken from the root. ሠናየ and አዳመ 'good' and 'pleasing' (accusative, predicates). The unit ends with ።, closing the paragraph.

sentences.t: ወባዕድኒ ፡ በዘ ፡ እነግረከ ፡ እምካልኣን ፡ ነቢያት ፡ በእንተ ፡ ስቅለቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-another-also, by-what I-tell-you from-other prophets concerning crucifixion-his;
sentences.i: And furthermore, in what I tell you from other prophets about his crucifixion;
sentences.n: A new paragraph: the chronicler now adds testimony from the prophets. ወባዕድኒ 'and another also / furthermore' (ወ- + ባዕድ 'other' + -ኒ). በዘ እነግረከ 'by (or in) what I tell you' (በ- + ዘ- 'what' + 1cs imperfect of ነገረ + -ከ 'you'), written as two words; እምካልኣን ነቢያት 'from other prophets' (እም- + ካልእ plural). The sentence stops at ፤ without a main verb, and the quotations follow.

sentences.t: ይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ቀነዉኒ ፡ እደውየ ፡ ወእገርየ ፡ ዝኒ ፡ ገሃደ ፡ አርአየ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ቅንዋተ ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወእገሪሁ ፤
sentences.l: Said David 'They-nailed-me my-hands and-my-feet'; this-also openly he-showed concerning nails-of his-hands and-his-feet;
sentences.i: David said, 'They pierced my hands and my feet' (Psalm 22:16 in the Hebrew numbering); this too he showed openly, concerning the nailing of his hands and feet;
sentences.n: Psalm 22:16 (21:17 in the Greek), read as a prophecy of the crucifixion. ቀነዉኒ 'they pierced / nailed me' (ቀነወ, 3mp perfect + -ኒ 'me'); እደውየ 'my hands', እገርየ 'my feet' (+ -የ 'my'). ዝኒ ገሃደ አርአየ 'this too he showed openly' (ገሃደ adverbial accusative, 'openly'; አርአየ 3ms perfect, causative of ርእየ), the subject being David. በእንተ ቅንዋተ 'concerning the nailing of' (construct); ወእገሪሁ 'and his feet' (singular used collectively).

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ አስተዩኒ ፡ ብሒአ ፡ ለጽምእየ ፡ ዘኒ ፡ ገሃደ ፡ አርአየ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሰረበ ፡ ብሒአ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ስሕተቱ ፡ ለአዳም ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said 'Give-me-to-drink vinegar for-my-thirst'; this-also openly he-showed that he-drank vinegar on-account-of error-his of-Adam;
sentences.i: And again he said, 'Give me vinegar to drink for my thirst' (Psalm 69:21); this too he showed openly, that he drank vinegar on account of Adam's error;
sentences.n: Psalm 69:21 (68:22 in the Greek), read as the vinegar offered on the cross (Matthew 27:48, John 19:29). አስተዩኒ 'give me to drink!' (imperative, 2mp or 2ms, causative of ሰትየ + -ኒ 'me'); ብሒአ 'vinegar' (accusative); ለጽምእየ 'for my thirst'. ዘኒ is printed here (earlier ዝኒ); it is glossed in earlier parts as 'moreover, also (?)', and here I read it as 'this too'. ሰረበ 'he drank, sipped' (3ms perfect); በእንተ ስሕተቱ ለአዳም 'on account of Adam's error' (ለ- naming the owner after the suffix -ሁ).

sentences.t: መንፈሰ ፡ ሕይወት ፡ ዘነፍሐ ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፡ ለአዳም ፡ ሰረበ ፡ ብሒአ ፡ ወእድ ፡ እንተ ፡ ሣረረታ ፡ ለምድር ፡ ተቀነወት ፡ ዘበእንቲአሁ ፡ ለአዳም ፡ ተትሒቶ ፡ ተወልደ ፡ አያያተ ፡ ገብር ፡ ነሢኦ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: Spirit-of life which-he-breathed upon-him, upon-Adam, he-drank vinegar, and-the-hand which founded-it the-earth was-nailed, he-who for-his-sake, for-Adam, having-humbled-himself was-born likeness-of servant, having-taken (it).
sentences.i: He who breathed the breath of life into Adam drank vinegar, and the hand that founded the earth was nailed; he who for Adam's sake humbled himself was born in the likeness of a servant, having taken it.
sentences.n: The paragraph and the part end here, with the closing ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ marks of the part (the five marks belong to this unit). መንፈሰ ሕይወት ዘነፍሐ ላዕሌሁ ለአዳም is fronted: 'the spirit of life which he breathed upon him, upon Adam' (Genesis 2:7), resumed by the subject of ሰረበ 'he drank'. ወእድ እንተ ሣረረታ ለምድር 'and the hand which founded the earth' (እንተ fem. relative; ሣረረታ 'founded it' is a form of a verb ሠረረ read as 'laid the foundation', lemma uncertain (?)); ተቀነወት 'was nailed' (3fs perfect, agreeing with እድ). ዘበእንቲአሁ ለአዳም 'who for his sake, for Adam' (the suffix on በእንቲአ- anticipated by ለአዳም); ተትሒቶ 'having humbled himself' (converb of ተትሕተ); አያያተ ገብር 'the likeness / form of a servant' (read as in Philippians 2:7 (?)); ነሢኦ 'having taken' (converb of ነሥአ).
